title: upgrade ignores flags that do not apply to its mode, and install ignores the vendor-only ones when publishing
body:
Found by the 2026-09-21 doc audit (finding K7).

`install` refused `--prefix` in VENDOR mode ("A flag that is meaningless in the mode you are actually in is a usage error, not something to ignore") and ignored the mirror: `--force`, `--name`, `--alias` and `--lang` while publishing. `upgrade` ignored all of them: `--prefix` in a project upgraded from the manifest's source while the operator believed they had named another, and `--from` or `--force` in devbin's own tree did nothing.

Fix: install refuses a VENDOR-only flag when publishing; upgrade refuses `--from` and `--force` in devbin's own tree and `--prefix` in a project; each message names the mode and the remedy, in install's shape. Tests: localinstall.bats, two arms, driven red at the parent commit. Fixture installs are under the test's tmpdir, so a red run could not publish anywhere real.


## Resolution

Fixed at `b11d0ec`, test driven red first at its parent commit. Full suite 1578/1579 at `ae3b200`: the one failing arm was environment-caused (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 exported in the running shell defeated readonlygit.bats' stale fixture, and its control arm caught it) and is green in a clean environment; that file is hardened at `ad86870`. Reviewed by vc against this issue; vc's mutants on 0099 and 0104 were killed. Ships in 0.1.4.
